newsitem.title: USA: Coke woos McDonald's in soda wars-NYT.
newsitem.headline: Coke woos McDonald's in soda wars-NYT.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co is seeking to banish soft drinks produced by Dr Pepper/Seven Up Inc from thousands of McDonald's Corp restaurants, the New York Times said.
In Tuesday's edition, the Times said Coca-Cola has offered so-called "exclusive awards" to McDonald's restaurants owners, including several thousand that carry the Dr Pepper brand.
Dr Pepper/Seven Up is a subsidiary of Cadbury Schweppes Plc .

In exchange for selling only Coca-Cola products, Coke has offered McDonald's franchisees between 200 and 600 free gallons of soda syrup for each restaurant, enough to make between 30,000 and 90,000 drinks per restaurant.
The Times said Dr Pepper/Seven Up Chief Executive Todd Stitzer declined to comment on the matter, which originally was reported in the industry newsletter, Beverage Digest.
